paragraphs: The new question is whether fairly tuning rho's permitted implementation and policy changes the comparison with retained degree-83 IC. The historical default strong-rho result is a measured default configuration, not a search certificate for the best possible rho implementation. The old packed reference remains inadmissible as the primary strong control.

The exact retained model is icv1-f2m83-t6151469093347-9eba6cd5, with polynomial low terms [0,2,4,7], subgroup order 8569786107849059 and the frozen legacy G/Q. The wrong-modulus cdcc5432 alias remains historical metadata only. Field degree 83, approximately 53-bit subgroup size, field representation and factor-base membership are distinct.

This new addendum leads the combined PDF. The prior 14-page default evaluation and the prior 48-page combined report retain their recorded numbers, sources and status. A new selected-policy result is separately source-bound and is never presented as a retiming of the old executable.

sections.title: Field backend and policy fairness
paragraphs: Every compared backend must preserve the exact field polynomial, subgroup, generator and public target binding. A different registered degree-83 modulus is a different coordinate instance, even when subgroup order agrees. Normal-basis conversion/canonicalization is an arithmetic representation choice, not a new factor base or relation-vector basis.

PENDING: name each measured field kernel, rho walk/collision policy and source/binary hash. State which changes apply to rho only and which are available to both rho and IC. Keep a shared field-kernel change distinct from a rho-only tuning result, and disclose any unequal implementation opportunity.

PENDING: state reusable-preparation, conversion, target-start, validation, walk/collision and replay boundaries for every selected arm. Charge target-dependent work online and retain conversion/setup costs separately. Shared mathematical invariants do not justify assuming equal runtime.

sections.title: Stop rules and complete cost boundaries
paragraphs: The new rho arms share a 60-second whole-process cap. IC has a 1800-second whole-process cap to accommodate reusable preparation. These are unequal stop envelopes; common CPU/memory settings must be separately documented. A censored or failed arm never counts as a performance win, and all attempted process costs remain records.

IC has no 20-million-probe cap. Its third command-line argument 29 is a rank seed. extract128 traverses the full index.states once; exhausting that finite cycle is an algorithmic termination, not an invented probe budget. Keep the actual whole-process timeout separate from extraction exhaustion and producer probe units.

Fresh-process IC cost begins with the retained base file. It measures base loading, root-index construction and rank/log work, but not original selection/construction of the 600 representatives. OS page cache is not flushed. Rho curve/normal-basis/jump construction is measured; supplied subgroup/catalog facts are not a newly timed discovery or factorization procedure.

PENDING: retain both producer phase residuals and the new runner's before-spawn/exit-observation boundaries exactly. Use native complete online intervals as declared, not silently corrected phase sums. Preserve child CPU and producer process timestamps alongside outer wall.
